title: Titus 3: regeneration needed that we may be justified
source_text: X. Tertius locus istius generis reperitur in epist. ad Titum, cap. 3. ubi dicitur quod Deus salvos nos fecit per lavacrum regenerationis, & renovationis Spiritus Sancti, quem effudit in nos abunde per Jesum Christum servatorem nostrum, ut justificati gratia ipsius, haeredes simus secundum spem vitae aeternae. Nam ut manifestum est, Apostolus ibi docet Deum nos regenerasse per Spiritum Sanctum, quem in nos abunde effudit; ut sic per gratiam ejus justificati, haereditatem vitae aeternae legitime sperare possimus; adeoque supponit necesse esse nos regenerari, & renovari per Spiritum, ut justificemur, quo sensu sumit ibi vocem justificationis. Si autem nobis opus est regeneratione, & interna per Spiritum Sanctum renovatione, ut pro justificatis apud Deum habeamur, certe justificatio ex mente Apostoli eo loco complectitur nostram sanctificationem.
pass_a_gloss: A third place of this kind is found in the epistle to Titus, chapter 3, where it is said that God made us safe through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior, that being justified by his grace we might be heirs according to the hope of eternal life. For as is manifest, the Apostle there teaches that God has regenerated us through the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly; that thus justified by his grace we might lawfully hope for the inheritance of eternal life; and so he presupposes that it is necessary that we be regenerated and renewed by the Spirit in order that we may be justified, in which sense he takes the word justification there. But if we need regeneration and inward renewal through the Holy Spirit in order to be held justified before God, certainly justification in the Apostle's mind in that place embraces our sanctification.
pass_b_english: Titus 3: God regenerates by the Spirit so that, justified by grace, we hope for life.
If regeneration is prerequisite to being counted justified, justification here includes sanctification.
